question.problem:
The mean weight of a group of newborn children is $3.2kg$ with a standard deviation of $350g.$
What is the $z$-score that corresponds to a weight of $3kg?$ Give your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $350g=0.350kg$

The $z$-score of an observation $x$ is defined by

$$
z=\frac{x-\overset{―}{x}}{\sigma }.
$$

The $z$-score represents how many standard deviations an observation is above or below the mean of the data set.

So, the $z$-score of the observation $x=3$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{x-\overset{¯}{x}}{\sigma } \\  & =\frac{3-3.2}{0.350} \\  & =-0.57\end{aligned}
$$

 
to $2$ decimal places.
